title: Pantheon, Rome
note: Hadrianic rotunda whose unreinforced concrete dome spans 43.3 m, equal to its height.

title: Great Mosque of Cordoba
note: Umayyad hypostyle hall with double-arched columns, later enlarged in four phases.

title: Hassan II Mosque, Casablanca
note: Modern mosque with a minaret about 210 m tall on an Atlantic platform.

title: Mortuary Temple of Hatshepsut, Deir el-Bahari
note: Terraced colonnaded temple cut into cliffs at Thebes, with published terrace dimensions.

title: Temple of Jupiter at Baalbek
note: Roman temple podium with trilithon blocks of about 800 tonnes and 22 m columns.

title: Masjid al-Haram and the Kaaba, Mecca
note: Cubic Kaaba about 13 m tall at the centre of the largest mosque complex.

title: Selimiye Mosque, Edirne
note: Sinan masterwork with a 31.25 m dome and four 83 m minarets.

title: Mount Nemrut tumulus of Antiochus I
note: Commagene royal tumulus about 50 m high flanked by colossal statues 8-9 m tall.

title: Meenakshi Temple, Madurai
note: Dravidian temple complex with fourteen gopurams, the tallest near 52 m.

title: Harmandir Sahib (Golden Temple), Amritsar
note: Central Sikh shrine within a sacred pool, with a documented plan and gilded dome.

title: Red Fort, Delhi
note: Mughal fortress-palace with 33 m walls and a plan of about 254 acres.

title: Gol Gumbaz, Bijapur
note: Tomb with one of the largest pre-modern domes, about 44 m in diameter.

title: Ajanta Caves
note: Thirty rock-cut Buddhist caves with murals and published plan dimensions.

title: Giant Wild Goose Pagoda, Xi'an
note: Tang brick pagoda built for Xuanzang's scriptures, about 64 m tall.

title: Ming Tombs, Beijing
note: Thirteen imperial tombs of the Ming with the Changling hall on a 1,950 m^2 platform and 32 columns.

title: Ananda Temple, Bagan
note: Mon-style cruciform temple with a spire about 51 m tall.

title: Phra Pathom Chedi
note: Tallest stupa in the world at about 120 m, built over an older Dvaravati core.

title: Kalyan Minaret, Bukhara
note: Karakhanid brick minaret 45.6 m tall with a documented base diameter.

title: Gur-e-Amir, Samarkand
note: Timurid mausoleum of Timur with a ribbed turquoise dome.

title: Kuelap fortress
note: Chachapoya walled citadel on a ridge, walls up to 20 m high and 600 m long.

title: Pyramid of the Niches, El Tajin
note: Six-tier pyramid with 365 niches, about 18 m high on a 36 m base.

title: Huaca del Sol, Moche
note: Adobe platform pyramid of the Moche, once about 40 m high and 340 m long.

title: Ciudad Perdida (Teyuna)
note: Tayrona terraced city in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta with a mapped plan.

title: Golden Gate Bridge
note: Suspension bridge with a 1,280 m main span and towers 227 m tall.

title: Hoover Dam
note: Concrete arch-gravity dam 221 m high and 379 m long on the Colorado River.

title: Empire State Building
note: Art Deco skyscraper 381 m to the roof, built in 410 days.

title: Poverty Point earthworks
note: Archaic concentric earthwork ridges and a mound about 22 m high in Louisiana.

title: Fort Jesus, Mombasa
note: Portuguese fort designed by Cairati with documented bastion plan on the Swahili coast.

title: Tomb of Askia, Gao
note: Songhai pyramidal mud-brick tomb about 17 m tall.

title: Ahu Tongariki
note: Largest ahu on Rapa Nui, with fifteen moai on a platform about 220 m long.

title: Leluh ruins, Kosrae
note: Basalt-walled island capital of Kosrae with royal compounds and canals.

title: Marco Polo's journey to Yuan China
note: Venice to Khanbaliq via Acre, Hormuz, Kashgar and Shangdu, 1271-1295.

title: Faxian's pilgrimage to India
note: Chang'an to Dunhuang, Khotan, Gandhara, Pataliputra and Ceylon, returning by sea in 412.

title: Lewis and Clark Expedition
note: St. Louis to Fort Mandan, Three Forks and Fort Clatsop, 1804-1806.

title: Trail of Tears
note: Forced removal of Cherokee along dated routes from Georgia to Indian Territory.

title: Burke and Wills expedition
note: Melbourne to Cooper Creek and the Gulf of Carpentaria with dated depots.

title: Livingstone's trans-African journey
note: Linyanti to Luanda and Quelimane, with Victoria Falls reached in 1855.

title: Bartolomeu Dias rounds the Cape
note: Lisbon to Mossel Bay and the Great Fish River, opening the sea route to India.

title: Orellana's descent of the Amazon
note: Quito to the Napo River and the Atlantic mouth of the Amazon, 1541-1542.

title: Balboa crosses the Isthmus of Panama
note: Santa Maria de la Antigua to the Pacific sighting on 25 September 1513.

title: Yijing's voyage to Srivijaya and India
note: Guangzhou to Srivijaya, Tamralipti and Nalanda, with return in 695.

title: Pytheas of Massalia's northern voyage
note: Massalia around Iberia and Britain to Thule, with described tin and amber stops.

title: Voyage of Hanno the Navigator
note: Carthaginian colonising voyage down the Atlantic African coast with named settlements.

title: Nearchus' voyage from the Indus to the Gulf
note: Alexander's fleet from Patala to Susa along the Makran coast, 325-324 BCE.

title: William of Rubruck's mission to the Mongols
note: Constantinople to Karakorum via the Volga and Sarai, with a detailed itinerary.

title: Trans-Siberian Railway
note: Railway from Chelyabinsk to Vladivostok built 1891-1916, with dated station segments.

title: Norse voyages to Vinland
note: Greenland to Helluland, Markland and L'Anse aux Meadows around 1000 CE.

title: Marinoan snowball Earth glaciation
note: Cryogenian global glaciation ending about 635 Ma with cap carbonates.

title: Vredefort impact
note: Largest verified impact structure, about 300 km across, in South Africa.

title: Sudbury impact
note: Paleoproterozoic impact creating the Sudbury nickel basin in Ontario.

title: Origin of land plants
note: Embryophytes colonised land in the Ordovician, shown by cryptospores.

title: Zanclean flood
note: Atlantic refilling of the Mediterranean after the Messinian crisis.

title: Middle Miocene climatic transition
note: Cooling and expansion of the East Antarctic ice sheet about 14 Ma.

title: Eemian interglacial
note: Last interglacial warm period with sea level several metres above today.

title: Toarcian oceanic anoxic event
note: Early Jurassic anoxia and extinction linked to Karoo-Ferrar volcanism.

title: 4.2 kiloyear event
note: Abrupt aridification about 2200 BCE linked to Akkadian and Old Kingdom collapse.

title: Ontong Java Plateau eruption
note: Largest known large igneous province, emplaced in the Cretaceous Pacific.

title: Year without a summer
note: Post-Tambora cooling caused crop failure in Europe and North America.

title: Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami
note: Magnitude 9.1 Sumatra rupture killing about 230,000 people in fourteen countries.

title: Tangshan earthquake
note: Magnitude 7.5 quake killing at least 240,000 people.

title: Mid-Pliocene warm period
note: Warm interval with CO2 near 400 ppm and sea level well above present.

title: Harriet Tubman
note: Escaped slave, Underground Railroad conductor, Union scout.

title: Sojourner Truth
note: Formerly enslaved abolitionist and women's rights speaker.

title: Sacagawea
note: Lemhi Shoshone interpreter who accompanied the Corps of Discovery.

title: Marie Curie
note: Discovered polonium and radium; two Nobel Prizes.

title: Ada Lovelace
note: Wrote the first published algorithm for Babbage's Analytical Engine.

title: Mary Seacole
note: Jamaican-born nurse and businesswoman who tended soldiers in the Crimean War.

title: Gaspar Yanga
note: Escaped enslaved leader whose maroons won recognition of San Lorenzo de los Negros.

title: Micaela Bastidas
note: Co-leader of the 1780 Tupac Amaru rebellion in Peru.

title: Li Qingzhao
note: Song dynasty poet, the most celebrated woman writer in classical Chinese.

title: Ching Shih
note: Former prostitute who commanded the Red Flag Fleet of about 1,800 ships.

title: Enheduanna
note: Akkadian high priestess and earliest named author in history.

title: Rabia al-Adawiyya
note: Former slave who became a foundational Sufi mystic of Basra.

title: Savitribai Phule
note: Opened the first girls' school in Pune in 1848 and campaigned against caste.

title: Pandita Ramabai
note: Sanskrit scholar and reformer who founded the Mukti Mission for widows.

title: Kartini
note: Javanese pioneer of women's education whose letters were published in 1911.

title: Nana Asma'u
note: Scholar and teacher of the Sokoto Caliphate who trained women teachers.

title: Tomyris
note: Massagetae queen who defeated and killed Cyrus the Great per Herodotus.

title: Truganini
note: Tasmanian Aboriginal woman who survived the Black War and became an icon of survival.

title: Whina Cooper
note: Maori leader who led the 1975 land march from Te Hapua to Wellington.

title: Vibia Perpetua
note: Carthaginian noblewoman martyr whose prison diary survives.

title: Printing of the Diamond Sutra
note: Oldest dated printed book, found at Dunhuang.

title: Invention of coinage in Lydia
note: First standardised electrum coins in Lydia, spreading across the Mediterranean.

title: House of Wisdom, Baghdad
note: Abbasid translation and research institution under al-Ma'mun.

title: Green Revolution in India
note: High-yield wheat and rice that averted famine, tied to Borlaug and Swaminathan.

title: Jiaozi paper money in Song China
note: First state-issued paper currency in Sichuan.

title: Launch of M-Pesa
note: Mobile money in Kenya that reached most adults and spread across Africa.

title: Wootz crucible steel in South Asia
note: High-carbon crucible steel produced in India, source of Damascus blades.

title: Guru Nanak and the founding of Sikhism
note: Nanak's revelation at Sultanpur and first Sikh community at Kartarpur.

title: Adi Shankara
note: Systematiser of Advaita Vedanta and founder of monastic centres.

title: Daodejing
note: Foundational Daoist text attributed to Laozi, with Guodian and Mawangdui manuscripts.

title: Declaration of the Bab
note: Shiraz proclamation that began the Babi movement and led to the Baha'i Faith.

title: Zoroaster
note: Prophet of Zoroastrianism whose Gathas anchor the Avesta.

title: British punitive expedition to Benin
note: Sack of Benin City and looting of the Benin Bronzes.

title: Ife bronze and terracotta heads
note: Naturalistic lost-wax heads from Ile-Ife, excavated 1938.

title: Mexican muralism movement
note: State-sponsored murals by Rivera, Orozco and Siqueiros after the Revolution.

title: Papunya Tula art movement
note: Western Desert acrylic painting that began Aboriginal contemporary art.

title: Code of Ur-Nammu
note: Oldest surviving law code, Sumerian and predating Hammurabi.

title: Corpus Juris Civilis
note: Justinian's codification of Roman law, basis of civil law traditions.

title: Nineteenth Amendment
note: US constitutional amendment granting women the vote.
